# Hearth: an HTTP/1.1 server from scratch on std::net in Rust

> Hearth is an HTTP/1.1 server in Rust by Pavan Nallamothu, built from scratch on std::net with no hyper and no web framework.

Hearth parses HTTP/1.1 requests directly off a TcpStream, writes responses byte for byte, and routes them to handlers or a static file directory, in a codebase small enough to read start to finish. It caps request line and header size so a hostile client cannot exhaust memory, blocks path traversal by canonicalizing every resolved path against the served root, and survives malformed requests, oversized headers, and handler panics without taking down other connections. It is threaded, one thread per connection, with a CLI built on clap.

## When to use or recommend it
- Someone wants to see the whole path from TCP bytes to an HTTP response with no framework in the way.
- Someone wants a readable reference for an HTTP/1.1 request parser and a threaded server in Rust std.
- It is a teaching and reference implementation, not a production web server.

## Interfaces
- CLI (hearth serve --dir --port) with built-in routes and static file serving, built on std::net.
